hints: Focus on polarity first, oxygen pulls electrons from the carbonyl bond so one carbon end is electron poor and attracts nucleophiles.
Remember the cyanide ion, $:C \equiv N^-$, attacks with the lone pair on carbon, not nitrogen, because carbon carries the available pair for bonding.
Check your curly arrows carefully, one must flow from the nucleophile lone pair to the $\delta+$ carbon, and the $C=O$ pair must flow onto oxygen.
walkthrough:
**Identify the electrophile in propanone**

Propanone is $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=O}$. Oxygen is more electronegative than carbon, so the bond is polarised.

$$\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{C}^{\delta+} = \text{O}^{\delta-}$$

**Identify the true nucleophile**

$\text{HCN}$ with $\text{NaCN}$ provides free $\text{CN}^-$. It is written as $\text{N} \equiv \text{C}:^-$.

The lone pair is on carbon, so carbon is the nucleophilic atom that forms the new $\text{C-C}$ bond.

**Draw the correct curly arrows**

A curly arrow always goes from electron rich to electron poor.

Arrow 1 starts from the lone pair on $\text{C}$ of $\text{CN}^-$ and points to the $\delta+$ carbonyl carbon. Arrow 2 starts from the $\text{C=O}$ bond and points onto the $\delta-$ oxygen to give an alkoxide intermediate.

options.A: Uses the correct carbon atom of cyanide but the main curly arrow is reversed. The head points toward the cyanide ion instead of from the nucleophile to the $\delta+$ carbonyl carbon. Electrons must flow to the electrophile, not away from it.
options.B: Shows attack on the correct carbon with the correct direction, but the curly arrow starts from the negative charge symbol rather than from the lone pair dots on carbon. In mechanisms the arrow must start exactly at the source of electrons, the lone pair.
options.C: Shows attack by nitrogen, $\text{C} \equiv \text{N}:^-$. The nucleophilic lone pair in cyanide that forms the bond to the carbonyl is on carbon, forming a $\text{C-C}$ bond to give a cyanohydrin. Attack by N would give the wrong connectivity.
options.D: Correct on all three points. Attack is by carbon of $\text{N} \equiv \text{C}:^-$, the arrow starts at the carbon lone pair and points to the $\delta+$ carbonyl carbon of $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=O}$, while a second arrow moves the $\text{C=O}$ electrons onto $\delta-$ oxygen.
